new_entities.name: Low-load blood-flow-restriction training
new_entities.description: Low-load resistance exercise performed with blood-flow restriction to preserve or rebuild muscle when heavy loading is difficult.

new_entities.name: Muscle hypertrophy during rehabilitation
new_entities.description: Restoration or increase of muscle size during rehabilitation after injury or surgery.

edges.effect_quant: Rehabilitation-focused evidence suggests low-load BFR can preserve or rebuild muscle size without requiring heavy loads. In ACL reconstruction rehabilitation, a 2025 meta-analysis of 245 patients found better strength and symptoms with BFR but variable effects on quadriceps muscle volume (SMD 0.28, P = 0.43). Direct trials still show clinically useful hypertrophy signals: after arthroscopic partial meniscectomy and ACL reconstruction, BFR groups improved quadriceps thickness more than routine rehabilitation alone, while matching heavy-load training for muscle-thickness gains in a National Health Service ACL cohort.
edges.population: patients in musculoskeletal rehabilitation, especially after knee surgery when heavy resistance loading is limited
edges.mechanism: Blood-flow restriction allows low mechanical loads to create a stronger hypertrophic stimulus, helping offset disuse atrophy when pain, healing tissue, or joint tolerance limits conventional high-load training.
edges.summary: This is one of the better-supported niche rehab tools in the batch. Low-load BFR is not magic, but it gives clinicians and athletes a credible way to chase hypertrophy and strength when standard heavy loading is too provocative or too early.
edges.caveats: The muscle-size effect is not uniformly superior in every review, and protocols differ widely in cuff pressure, frequency, and exercise selection. It is best framed as a useful substitute or bridge, not a universal replacement for later-stage heavy loading.

evidence.notes: Blood Flow Restriction Enhances Recovery After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

Comparing the Effectiveness of Blood Flow Restriction and Traditional Heavy Load Resistance Training in the Post-Surgery Rehabilitation of Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Patients: A UK National Health Service Randomised Controlled Trial.
